claims.text: UTMB Health announced that artificial intelligence now supports its lung cancer screening work.

claims.document: UTMB Health, AI adds a new layer of support to lung cancer screening at UTMB Health

claims.text: UTMB Health started its screening program in 2016 for patients at high risk of lung cancer.
claims.quote: UTMB Health established the program in 2016 to screen patients who are at high risk for lung cancer
claims.document: UTMB Health, AI adds a new layer of support to lung cancer screening at UTMB Health

claims.document: UTMB Health, AI adds a new layer of support to lung cancer screening at UTMB Health

rejected.reason: The UTMB release states no accuracy, sensitivity or error figure for the nodule flagging system. Its only accuracy wording (c24) is about robotic bronchoscopy biopsies.

rejected.finding: Counts of patients, scans or nodules
rejected.reason: The release gives no totals. Two thirds (c17) is a share with no denominator.

rejected.finding: Time to follow up after adoption
rejected.reason: The release gives only the old delay (c5). Bunkerhill's 80 percent (c25) is the vendor's claim with no baseline and must never read as UTMB's measured result.

rejected.finding: Bunkerhill's other figures (time savings, outreach hours, reviews per month, navigator count)
rejected.reason: Vendor marketing figures with no stated period or baseline. Kept out.

rejected.finding: The validated risk score is the Brock score
rejected.reason: UTMB names no score. Bunkerhill names Brock (c26). Treating them as the same is an inference neither page states.

rejected.finding: Robotic bronchoscopy is part of the Bunkerhill system
rejected.reason: Not stated. It is a separate tool in Dr. Nishi's account.

rejected.finding: Galveston County named in the release
rejected.reason: The release body names no county. Galveston comes from the docket item, where UTMB's main campus sits.
